title: Parallel and Identical Lines
short: Spot systems with no solution or infinitely many.

blocks.html: Two lines don’t always cross. This lesson joins substitution with what you learned about equations with no solution or infinitely many.

Two lines in a plane can do only three things: cross once, never meet (parallel: same slope, different $y$-intercepts), or lie on top of each other (the same line). Algebra tells the same story: substitution ends with $x$ = a number, with a false statement, or with a true statement.

Write both equations as $y = mx + b$. Different slopes: one solution. Same slope and different intercepts: no solution. Same slope and same intercept: infinitely many solutions (every point on the line).

blocks.name: linesystem
blocks.cap: Use the sliders. Then try to make infinitely many solutions.

blocks.title: Parallel lines
steps: Rewrite the second: $-2y = -6x + 8$, so $y = 3x - 4$. Same slope 3, different intercepts: parallel.
Algebra agrees: $6x - 2(3x + 2) = 8$ gives $-4 = 8$, which is false.

blocks.title: The same line
steps: Rewrite the second: $2y = -2x + 8$, so $y = -x + 4$. It is the same line.
Every point on it works, such as $(0, 4)$ and $(1, 3)$.

blocks.title: Tell at a glance
blocks.q: How many solutions do $y = 2x + 1$ and $y = -2x + 1$ have?
steps: The slopes, 2 and $-2$, are different, so the lines cross once (here at $(0, 1)$).

blocks.html: Thinking “infinitely many solutions” means every pair $(x, y)$ works. Only points on the shared line do: $(0, 0)$ is not a solution of $y = -x + 4$.
